beats.care: If family or friends live in Saudi Arabia, India's embassy asks them to stay indoors. Its free helpline is 800 247 1234.
beats.what: Houthi rebels from Yemen fired a missile at Riyadh's main airport on 8 October. Saudi officials say three people were killed, including a pilot.
beats.why: The Houthis call it revenge for Saudi strikes on Yemen's airports. Their war flared again after the US and Israel attacked Iran.

cards.body: Saudi aviation officials say the 8 Oct strike on King Khalid Airport killed a Saudia pilot and two other Saudi citizens, and wounded dozens. Earlier attacks hit Abha, Jazan and Najran airports. The Houthis warned airlines to avoid Saudi airspace. Riyadh airport has since reopened.
Run by the embassy's Pravasi Bharatiya Sahayata Kendra; updates are also posted on X at @IndianEmbRiyadh.
cards.caption: Free 24x7 helpline for Indians in Saudi Arabia

cards.body: An armed group that controls much of northern Yemen, including the capital Sanaa. Iran backs them. A Saudi-led coalition has fought them since 2015. That war was mostly frozen for years, then reignited after the US and Israel's war on Iran.
cards.title: who are the houthis?

cards.body: India's foreign ministry condemned the attacks on Abha and Riyadh airports, calling the targeting of civilian sites 'completely unacceptable'. Air India cancelled Riyadh flights until 10 Oct, and Akasa and Saudia flights from Kochi to Riyadh were cancelled.
